newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - March 18.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- SHARES AND POUND FALL ON ELECTION FEARS

Investors reacted nervously yesterday on news of a May 1 general election. Share prices and the pound both fell sharply. The prospect of a Labour victory, although on the cards for a while, sparked a rush by investors to take profits after the gains made since last summer. The heavy selling of British shares and bonds contributed to the slide in sterling.
-- SCARDINO REFUSES TO BE PUSHED OVER DISPOSALS AT PEARSON

Marjorie Scardino, the new chief executive at Pearson, yesterday promised to improve her performance at Pearson with tougher revenue and cash targets. She said change would be through evolution and not revolution and she would not be pushed into making disposals just to keep the City sweet.
-- ENGLISH CHINA PLUNGES 43 MILLION POUNDS STG INTO THE RED

English China Clays reported yesterday it had fallen into the red and cut its dividend, but it believed the worst was over. The company lost 43 million stg compared with a 95 million stg pre-tax profit last year. The company incurred a 10 million stg restructuring charge and an 85 million stg write down of assets, including a 58 million stg charge against Kaolin clay reserves held by Middle Georgia.
THE TIMES
-- JUDGES QUASH CONVICTION OF NADIR AIDE

The Serious Fraud Office was defeated yesterday when the Court of Appeal overturned the case against Elizabeth Forsyth, the one time aide to Asil Nadir. Forsyth had served 10 months in prison of a five year sentence for handling almost 400,000 stg in allegedly stolen funds. She has accused the SFO of ruining her life and will seek compensation after the Court of Appeal quashed her the conviction, saying the trial judge had misdirected the jury on two occasions.
-- IBM PAYS STAFF RECORD BONUS

The computer company, IBM is to pay its staff a record $1.2 billion as part of an incentive scheme. The company's 241,000 employees around the world will receive an average of $4,979. Last year, IBM made profits of $5.9 billion.
-- LONRHO FALLS AS MARKET REACTS TO WARNING

Shares in Lonrho fell by 8 percent yesterday following a warning given by the company that interim profits could be down by a third on last year. The company cited the strength of sterling, lower precious metal prices, disappointing earnings from the Ashanti mines and moderate results at its African trading businesses as factors for the decline in profits.
THE GUARDIAN
-- LANG HASTENS GAS FREE-FOR-ALL

Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang yesterday pledged that consumers nationwide could feel the benefits of competition as early as April 1998 when all 19 million domestic gas users will be able to choose their supplier. Lang announced that ahead of the introduction of competition nationally the third phase of the process will take in around 2.5 million consumers in Scotland and the Northeast.
-- BAe SET TO WIN 300 MILLION STG GUNS ORDER

Britain's arms industry is set to win a 300 million stg order for specialised lightweight artillery from the US Marine Corps. Royal Ordnance, the British Aerospace subsidiary, is competing with GEC's VSEL to supply artillery and is expecting an announcement from the Pentagon today. It is the second boost for the UK defence industry in two days. The United Arab Emirates announced yesterday it wants to evaluate the four- nation Eurofighter 2000 alongside rival French and US aircraft in what could be a 40-jet order.
-- CO-OP CHIEF MOUNTS ATTACK ON BESIEGER

Lancia, the investment trust seeking to break up the Co-op, is coming under increasing pressure to publish a realistic proposal or abandon its attempts. The stock exchange is considering the Co-op's complaints that suspension of its stock is no longer valid. Lancia's creditability as a potential bidder is also being undermined by its complex ownership structure, involving several investment vehicles based in Monaco and the West Indies.
THE INDEPENDENT
LUARD IN LINE FOR 6 MILLION STG WINDFALL AS FLEXTECH SIGNS BBC DEAL

Flextech's chief executive Roger Luard is set to net more than 6 million stg from the sale of shares and the exercise of options in the satellite and cable broadcaster, which yesterday announced details of its pay-TV joint venture with the BBC.
-- ARGOS PREPARES FOR 1 BILLION STG SPENDING SPREE

Argos reported yesterday it was prepared to spend as much as 1 billion stg on a UK acquisition. Mike Smith, chief executive of the catalogue retailer, would not comment on possible interest in the Littlewoods high street stores but said he would be prepared to look at something in the furniture, sports or leisure markets, as well as a list of targets in the toys, electrical and jewellery markets.
-- TYCO SECURES ADT WITH $5.6 BILLION FRIENDLY OFFER

A friendly offer of $5.6 billion from Tyco International seems to have ended the bitter battle for control of ADT, the burglar alarm company. The deal has been approved by the Tyco and ADT boards and is a blow to Western Resources, which had been struggling since last year to make ground with its hostile bid of 3.5 billion dollars US. Fire and safety systems maker Tyco agreed to play white knight by offering ADT shareholders $29 a share.
